key_insight: MedCORE makes image diagnosis more interpretable by explicitly reasoning over clinician-defined criteria, linking each criterion to image evidence and combining them with uncertainty-aware weighting.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians better understand why a model predicts a diagnosis across different medical imaging tasks, potentially supporting safer review and adoption.
method: Decomposes each diagnosis into clinically defined criteria and localizes evidence in relevant image regions.
Uses multi-scale feature encoding plus a graph attention network to model relationships among criteria.
Aligns criterion evidence with clinical text and class prototypes, then weights predictions by uncertainty.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on ISIC 2018, BUSI, and IDRiD, achieving 89.2%/85.7%/96.4% on ISIC, 96.1%/95.2%/98.4% on BUSI, and 84.3%/80.2%/92.8% on IDRiD for accuracy/macro-F1/AUC respectively.
watch_item: Performance looks strong in retrospective benchmarks, but clinical usefulness still depends on external validation, robustness across sites/scanners, and reliable criterion localization.
paper_title: MedCORE: Criteria-Grounded Clinical Reasoning for Interpretable Medical Image Diagnosis
